scope: Static publication/provenance evidence only. No solver execution, no protected-result opening, no Level-B change, no Korkin-gate authorization.

target.paper: Korkin et al. (2022), Numerical results for polarized light scattering in a spherical atmosphere
target.case: multiple scattering, uniform layer, OT=0.25, cos(SZA)=0.1

evidence.claim: The accepted manuscript reports Table 9(a) values for MYSTIC, MCSSA and VLIDORT under the frozen OT=0.25, cos(SZA)=0.1 case. The manuscript also identifies I(mu0,mu,phi) as total intensity when discussing the Adams-and-Kattawar benchmark lineage.
evidence.limitation: No explicit sentence tying Table 9(a) I to a stated incident-flux normalization has yet been recovered.

evidence.kind: independent published reproduction of Adams-and-Kattawar benchmark
evidence.claim: Figure 5 compares McSCIA points with Adams and Kattawar (1978) lines for the homogeneous conservative Rayleigh OT=0.25 spherical-shell benchmark and explicitly states that the plotted quantity is normalized radiance for an incoming solar flux of pi.
evidence.limitation: This establishes the Adams-and-Kattawar benchmark convention, not by itself the normalization of Korkin 2022 Table 9(a).

evidence.claim: Korkin et al. (2020) states that MYSTIC/VLIDORT reproduced with better accuracy and extended the Adams-and-Kattawar benchmark results.
evidence.limitation: No explicit normalization sentence from the 2020 paper has yet been recovered.

evidence.claim: The Eradiate publication states that its fully spherical implementation was validated against Korkin et al. (2022), and describes spherical-example radiances as normalized to incident solar irradiance.
evidence.limitation: The publication does not explicitly say that Korkin Table 9(a) itself uses the identical normalization.

evidence.claim: The archived companion spherical notebook sets directional illumination irradiance=1.0, uses spherical_shell + VolPathIntegrator, reads result.radiance directly, and labels the plotted quantity Normalized Radiance [—], with no post-run pi/mu0 scaling visible in the notebook.
evidence.limitation: This proves the Eradiate-side raw-output convention for that companion example, not the missing Korkin Table 9(a) author-side normalization statement.

newConstraint.adamsKattawarConvention: normalized radiance for incoming solar flux pi
newConstraint.eradiateRawUnitIrradianceConvention: raw radiance under directional irradiance=1.0 is treated as dimensionless normalized radiance in the publication companion
newConstraint.reason: The two convention chains are mutually compatible, but an explicit publication-authoritative bridge from Korkin 2022 Table 9(a) I to either convention is still missing. Matching numerical magnitude is forbidden as a bridge.

mayResolveOnlyWith: explicit Korkin 2022 manuscript/table/supplement statement of the incident-flux or radiance normalization
publication-authored Korkin 2022 validation/input artifact that unambiguously defines the Table 9(a) normalization
an equivalently direct author-side provenance chain that fixes all multiplicative factors without numerical fitting

nextAction: Continue exact author-side normalization recovery from Korkin 2022 accepted-manuscript machine text, supplementary ScienceDirect archive, or publication-authored benchmark artifacts. If an exact bridge is recovered, preregister it before any Korkin execution.
